title: RAGChecker: A Fine-grained Framework for Diagnosing Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Ru, Dongyu; Qiu, Lin; Hu, Xiangkun; Zhang, Tianhang; Shi, Peng; Chang, Shuaichen (shared first authorship); Jiayang, Cheng; Wang, Cunxiang; Sun, Shichao; Li, Huanyu; Zhang, Zizhao; Wang, Binjie; Jiang, Jiarong; He, Tong; Wang, Zhiguo; Liu, Pengfei; Zhang, Yue; Zhang, Zheng (Amazon AWS AI / Shanghai Jiaotong Univ. / Westlake Univ.)
venue_or_status: NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks Track (peer-reviewed); Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37, pp. 21999-22027; VERIFIED at proceedings.neurips.cc 2026-11-10 (record + BibTeX + official PDF); DOI 10.52202/079017-0692; arXiv 2408.08067 was the preprint
research_question: How to diagnose retrieval vs generation failures in RAG with fine-grained metrics?
method: Claim-level binary entailment evaluation: RefChecker-based text-to-claim extractor + claim-entailment checker (both Llama3-70B-Instruct); inputs are (query, chunked corpus, COMPLETE ground-truth answer); chunks classified relevant/irrelevant by whether they entail any gt claim; 'incorrect claim' DEFINED as response claim not entailed by gt (reference-anchored, not world-truth); no citations as inputs, no abstention handling; meta-evaluation = 280 pairwise human preferences (28 system pairs x 10 domains, 2 annotators each, 10 annotators)
model: Judge: Llama3-70B-Instruct as extractor+checker (validated on RefChecker benchmark: 91.89/71.75/78.35% accuracy in zero/noisy/accurate context, Table 16). Evaluated systems: {BM25, E5-Mistral} x {GPT-4, Llama3-8B, Llama3-70B, Mixtral-8x7B}, temp 0.0, top-20 chunks of 300 tokens
dataset_or_corpus: Own benchmark: 4,162 queries / 10 domains repurposed from RobustQA (7 domains incl. BioASQ, FiQA, LoTTE), ClapNQ, NovelQA, KIWI (Table 1); long-form gold answers for 6 RobustQA domains + NovelQA are GPT-4-GENERATED from human short answers + gold passages, RefChecker-filtered (App. A); data released (S3, CC) + code Apache-2.0
metrics: Exact formulas in App. B: overall Precision/Recall/F1 vs gt claims; retriever Claim Recall (gt claims entailed in retrieved context - RETRIEVAL-SIDE) + Context Precision (chunk-level); generator Faithfulness (response claims entailed in context), Relevant/Irrelevant Noise Sensitivity, Hallucination (not in gt AND not in context), Self-knowledge (in gt, not in context), Context Utilization. All LLM-judged, binary entailment, no partial support
main_findings: Meta-eval: best human correlation of 13 metrics (Pearson 49.66/60.67/61.93 correctness/completeness/overall vs human ceiling 63.67/71.91/70.09; RAGAS Answer Similarity next at 41.07/53.16/48.31; grounding metrics correlate poorly with correctness: RAGAS Faithfulness 8.22) (Tables 2/5); best system E5-Mistral_GPT-4 (F1 52.7, CR 83.5, Faith. 92.9) (Table 3); claim-recall/noise-sensitivity trade-off; relevant >> irrelevant noise sensitivity (chunk-level trust); open-source models trust context blindly; settings: more/larger chunks raise CR+faithfulness but also noise sensitivity; overlap ratio negligible (Sec. 4.4)
limitations: Author-stated (App. H): retriever metrics shallow; Neutral vs Contradiction checker outcomes NOT differentiated (unsupported = contradicted); benchmark English text-only, repurposed not RAG-native. Observed: all metrics conditional on gt completeness ('incorrect' = not-in-gt, so true extra claims count as noise/hallucination); per-claim judge error ~22-28% in context settings (Table 16); meta-eval validates RANKING correlation, not per-claim labels; annotators shown GPT-4 critiques (anchoring risk); gt for 6/10 domains GPT-4-written while GPT-4 is also evaluated (circularity risk); no variance/CIs; judge decoding settings and abstention handling not reported; no standards/telecom domain
trust_dimensions: evidence faithfulness (automatic, vs whole retrieved context); answer completeness vs gold; noise robustness diagnostics; NO citation correctness, NO abstention, NO version/modality
evidence_intervention: no (observational; Sec. 4.4 varies k/chunk-size/overlap/prompt, i.e. system hyperparameters, not evidence conditions)
relevance_to_nr_specrag: THE automated-evaluation baseline our human claim-level gold must position against, and the natural instantiation of our auxiliary LLM-judge track (open-source, judge-swappable); its three structural dependencies (gt completeness, binary support, judge error) are exactly what our required-facts + partial/materiality + human-gold design removes; also the framework behind every TelcoAI number
notes: seed 4; FULL-TEXT REVIEWED 2026-11-10 from official proceedings.neurips.cc PDF (pypdf extraction, 29/29 pages incl. App. A-I); detailed review: docs/research/full_text_reviews/ragchecker.md; Phase-1 'papers.nips.cc connection refused' blocker resolved via proceedings.neurips.cc; venue claim from TelcoAI's reference list now PRIMARY-verified; App. F radar figures read via prose only
closest_prior_work: automated-evaluation baseline for C3/C4 framing; evaluation framework used by telcoai-2025
delta_vs_nr_specrag: CONFIRMED from full text: automatic binary claim-entailment vs whole context/gt with LLM judge; no citation resolution or per-(claim,citation) verdicts (citations not an input), no partial-support/materiality, no contradicted-vs-unsupported split, no abstention/coverage, no version or modality dimension, no human claim-level gold (human data = 280 pairwise preferences), no statistical inference. title: VersionRAG: Version-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Evolving Documents
authors: Huwiler, Daniel; Stockinger, Kurt; Fürst, Jonathan (Zurich University of Applied Sciences)
venue_or_status: arXiv preprint 2510.08109 (v1 only, 2025-10-09, cs.IR); no DOI/journal ref and no venue acceptance found as of 2026-11-10 - not peer-reviewed; ACL-style template; App. B.1 says results come 'from the thesis evaluation'
domain: versioned-document QA (software docs/changelogs: Node.js, Apache Spark, Bootstrap; NOT telecom/3GPP)
research_question: Can explicit graph modelling of version sequences, content boundaries and inter-version changes fix RAG failures on versioned documents at low indexing cost?
method: Five-level version-aware graph (category/document/version/content/change nodes) in Neo4j + Milvus Lite vectors; indexing: LLM attribute extraction (title/version/type from first pages), LLM clustering, 512-token chunks w/ 50 overlap + version metadata, change extraction = LLM over changelogs (explicit) + DeepDiff line diffs between consecutive versions with LLM interpretation (implicit); retrieval: LLM query classification into content/version/change intents (92% acc DeepSeek, Table 8) + parameter extraction, then graph traversal or version-filtered vector search (filter BEFORE/DURING retrieval); generation grounded on pre-filtered version-specific context; few-shot prompts, no fine-tuning; NO citations, NO abstention
model: Llama 3 8B, GPT-4o Mini, DeepSeek-R1 70B (same LLM for indexing+generation per config; GroqCloud/OpenAI APIs); text-embedding-3-small; judge: GPT-4.1
dataset_or_corpus: VersionQA (released, github.com/danielhuwiler/versionrag - repo existence verified 2026-11-10, NO license file, contents not inspected): 100 author-curated QA pairs over 34 files/~710 pages: Spark changelogs 2.4.7-3.5.5 (6), Bootstrap changelogs 5.2.3-5.3.5 (6), Node.js Assert docs 11.15.0-23.11.0 (13), Node.js Errors 15.14.0-23.11.0 (9); 6 categories (20/20/20/20/10/10), 60% version-sensitive; gold = answers only, NO evidence spans; no annotator details/IAA; implicit-change gold is corpus-relative (CallTracker 'introduced 14.21.3' vs real v14.2.0/v12.19.0 per nodejs.org - unstated in paper)
metrics: Answer accuracy only (GPT-4.1 LLM judge vs gold, 'manually reviewed for all 100 questions', no judge-accuracy stats/IAA); indexing tokens/cost/time; NO retrieval metrics, NO faithfulness, NO citation metrics, NO abstention, no CIs/significance (sec 5.2: dataset size 'precludes extensive statistical testing')
main_findings: Overall accuracy (Table 5): VersionRAG 90/79/55 vs naive 58/53/47 vs GraphRAG 64/57/43 (DeepSeek/GPT-4o-Mini/Llama); version-specific content retrieval 100 vs 55 (DeepSeek, Table 7); implicit change detection 60 vs 0-10; indexing 186K vs 2,970K input tokens = 93.7% fewer (headline '97%' holds for input+output: 224K vs 8,892K), $0.17 vs $6.67, 25min vs 5h12; failure modes (App D.3 p.19, fractions of ALL 100 queries): naive fails 42 - version mixing 25, no change awareness 17; GraphRAG fails 36 - version confusion 20, missing change detection 16; VersionRAG fails 10 - misclassification 8, missed changes 2
limitations: Author (p.9): 100q/34docs precludes stats; tech-docs domain only; DeepDiff misses semantic-only changes; assumes extractable version ids + consistent structure + semantic versioning; no non-adjacent-version dependencies; no calendar-time reasoning; pipeline error propagation. Reviewer: Table 7 GraphRAG/DeepSeek CR-VS prints 100.0 but only 45.0 reconciles Table 5 (likely typo; dangling 'Section 4.2.3' ref); corpus-relative implicit-change gold unstated; 25% attribution has no coding protocol/second annotator/per-item labels; query-time LLM calls unmatched vs baselines; single run, no variance; dataset unlicensed
trust_dimensions: version-conditional grounding at answer-accuracy level; factual correctness; aggregate post-hoc error attribution (version mixing); no per-answer attribution, faithfulness, citation, abstention or modality measurement
evidence_intervention: no (retrieval-architecture change; version filtering prevents contamination by construction rather than evaluating behaviour under supplied evidence)
relevance_to_nr_specrag: THE strongest measured C1 prior (full-text confirmed): establishes versioned-doc QA task + public benchmark, measures version-sensitive accuracy, quantifies aggregate version mixing (25/100 naive-RAG queries) and its architectural remedy; but single-axis (question-type) evaluation over naturally-distributed evidence - correct answers grounded in wrong-version evidence are invisible to its metric, exactly what VFR/VAA/E4 measure; charter C1 falsifier NOT triggered (no version-attribution metric reported)
notes: FULL-TEXT REVIEWED 2026-11-10 from official arXiv PDF (pypdf, 25/25 pages incl. App A-F; file(1) miscount harmless); detailed review: docs/research/full_text_reviews/versionrag.md; supersedes S-12 partial_body stage via FT-05; CORRECTS Phase-1 note: version mixing = 25% of ALL queries (= 59.5% of naive-RAG's 42 errors), NOT 25% of errors; author spelling Fürst (umlaut) canonical; new citation-chase lead CH-11 (HoH); re-check publication status before thesis citation

title: HoH: A Dynamic Benchmark for Evaluating the Impact of Outdated Information on Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Ouyang, Jie; Pan, Tingyue; Cheng, Mingyue; Yan, Ruiran; Luo, Yucong; Lin, Jiaying; Liu, Qi (State Key Lab of Cognitive Intelligence, University of Science and Technology of China)
venue_or_status: ACL 2025 Long Papers (PEER-REVIEWED), pp.6036-6063, DOI 10.18653/v1/2025.acl-long.301, Vienna July 2025, ISBN 979-8-89176-251-0; arXiv 2503.04800 (v1 2025-03-03, last updated 2025-07-18); ACL version reviewed; abstracts identical, full version diff not performed
domain: present-anchored temporal QA over Wikipedia (encyclopedic facts; NOT telecom/3GPP, NOT normative text)
research_question: How does outdated information coexisting in retrieval sources degrade RAG retrieval and generation, and can models distinguish current from outdated evidence?
method: HOH-QA: Myers sentence diff + token-level diff marking + heuristic filters + fine-tuned Qwen2.5-0.5B factual-change screener (96.80% acc/95.08 F1, Table 7) + Llama-3.1-70B QA generation requiring CONTRADICTORY old/new answers + 5-criterion LLM quality review incl. Temporal Independence (forbids time-situated phrasing); monthly Wikipedia snapshots 2024-06..2024-11; answer chains preserve outdated answers+evidence+timestamps. HOH-SearchEngine: Elasticsearch BM25 + Gaussian temporal decay over current+historical article versions. Experiments: end-to-end RAG (bge-m3, k=20, top-5, time-aware prompt with current date + per-doc Last Modified) AND CONTROLLED fixed-context generation {R x1,D xn}, {R x1,O x1,D xn} with Score/Date-desc/Date-asc ordering, {O x1,D xn}; vanilla no-retrieval; AC/AO timeliness-awareness probes
model: Generators: Llama-3.1-70B/8B-Instruct, Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct (bfloat16, vLLM, temp 0.3, max 100 tok); GPT-4o on 1,000-sample subset (App E.3); retrieval: bge-base-en-v1.5, bge-m3, bge-reranker-v2-m3; judge: Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (also an evaluated generator)
dataset_or_corpus: HOH: 96,124 QA pairs + 219,463 documents (current + historical versions); every question has >=1 annotated outdated answer (Table 11: 91,856 one, up to 5); domains Sports 31.2%/Open 33.0%/Finance 23.7%/Movie 6.3%/Music 5.8%; eval subset 10,000 (10 clusters x 1,000); 3 annotators labelled 2,000 screener-training pairs (no IAA stat); 500-pair manual QA validation 98.4-100% (Table 9); public github.com/0russwest0/HoH (NOT inspected)
metrics: Answer-level 3-way Perfect(+1)/Missing(0)/Harmful(-1), Score=mean (CRAG-style, Yang et al. 2024b); judge rule: match gold current answer->Correct, explicit unsure->Unsure, ELSE Harmful (outdated answer never consulted); judge manually validated near-perfect (Table 13) but N unstated; retrieval HR@k for R and O separately; AC/AO probes; no CIs/significance
main_findings: End-to-end scores 51.7/40.0/29.9 (Llama-70B/8B/Qwen-7B, Fig.3). Retrieval: no decay O@5 0.8837 > R@5 0.8707; Gaussian decay O@5 0.4950 at cost R@5 0.7023 (-17%) (Table 2); embeddings keep O hit >50% (Table 3); MRAG/TempRALM suppress O only by crushing R (Table 15). Controlled generation: distractors mild (89.12->87.98, Table 4); ONE outdated passage severe (Llama-70B 89.12->63.9-67.0, harmful 4.1->14-16%, Table 5); O-only: harmful 67-83%, scores -58..-71 (Table 18); ordering swings Qwen-7B >50 pts incl. -2.77 (Date-desc n=5); vanilla: Missing 62-97% = appropriate uncertainty (Table 14); AC/AO awareness correlates with outcomes (Table 6); GPT-4o equally vulnerable (Tables 16-17)
limitations: Author (sec 7): fixed snapshot frequency; single-article QA; homogenized outdated corpus (historical versions of same article). Reviewer: present-anchored ONLY - old targets structurally absent (Temporal Independence criterion); correctness = match current gold (recency-anchored), never version-conditional; harmful never coded against the annotated outdated answer; judge self-judges Llama-70B rows; judge-validation/manual-QA Ns and annotator counts partly unstated, no IAA; no uncertainty quantification; Fig.3 values unreadable in text layer; minor prose/table drift ('11%' vs 12.69pp); article-level last-modified conflates edit time with fact validity
trust_dimensions: evidence-conditioned outcome rates (perfect/missing/harmful) under CONTROLLED current-vs-outdated evidence mixtures and ordering; retrieval-stage temporal contamination (R/O hit rates); abstention as scored outcome; staleness-awareness probes; NO citations, NO claim-level coding, NO per-answer version attribution, NO modality
evidence_intervention: yes, evaluation-side: fixed-context construction {R,O,D counts + ordering} is a controlled evidence-condition design (current-target half only); retrieval-side interventions (Gaussian decay, MRAG, TempRALM) evaluated on R/O hit rates as negative results
abstention_evaluation: partial: 'Unsure' instructed and SCORED 0 in the primary metric (scheme favors omission over error, sec 4.4); missing-rates reported per condition (62-97% vanilla); no calibration, selective-risk, coverage, or abstention-correctness analysis
relevance_to_nr_specrag: Strongest controlled-evidence prior for C1 (resolves CH-11): directly evaluates our cells B, D, F (current-target half) at outcome level with real revision conflicts; first reviewed paper scoring abstention in its primary metric (C4-adjacent). C1 wording must no longer claim 'first controlled current-vs-outdated evidence conditions'; remaining delta = symmetric old-target axis + per-answer/citation version attribution + behaviour coding + normative 3GPP domain
notes: FULL-TEXT REVIEWED 2026-11-10 from official ACL Anthology PDF (pypdf, 28/28 pages incl. App A-E and prompt figures; Fig.3 values CID-garbled - prose used); detailed review: docs/research/full_text_reviews/hoh.md; resolves CH-11 via FT-06; bibliography primary-verified via Anthology BibTeX; new citation-chase lead CH-12 (CLARK-News, only other outdated-info-annotated benchmark per its Table 1); repo NOT inspected

title: Language Modeling with Editable External Knowledge
authors: Li, Belinda Z. (MIT CSAIL); Liu, Emmy (CMU LTI); Ross, Alexis (MIT CSAIL); Zeitoun, Abbas (MIT CSAIL); Neubig, Graham (CMU LTI); Andreas, Jacob (MIT CSAIL)
venue_or_status: Findings of ACL: NAACL 2025 (PEER-REVIEWED), pp.3070-3090, DOI 10.18653/v1/2025.findings-naacl.168, Albuquerque April 29-May 4 2025, ISBN 979-8-89176-195-7; arXiv 2406.11830 (v1-only, 2024-06-17); NAACL camera-ready reviewed; camera-ready ADDS Table 2 (Self-RAG stack) and Table 4 (forgetting/old-target probe) absent from arXiv v1
domain: streaming news temporal QA + synthetic persona conversations (Wikidata-derived facts; NOT telecom/3GPP, NOT normative text)
research_question: Can editing an external knowledge base at document-insertion time (deleting/rewriting affected entries as each document arrives) keep RAG answers accurate as facts change over a chronological document stream, better than appending to the store and resolving conflicts at query time?
method: ERASE (Enhancing Retrieval Augmentation with Self-consistent Editing): KB entries = (fact, truth-history [(timestamp,truth-value)...]); per new document: GTR-retrieve related facts (sim>0.7) -> classify reinforce/no-change/make-false (conservative default: keep true if not contradicted) -> rewrite false facts conditioned on doc + still-true facts (enables multi-hop edits, partial-falsity salvage) -> add extracted atomic current-state facts; prediction = standard RAG over edited KB with truth histories shown in prompt. Benchmark CLARK: News (real articles, 2 Prolific rounds + 1 LM filter) and Conversations (synthetic Markov-chain worlds, 12-chunk LLM persona dialogues, single-hop vs multi-hop subsets)
model: Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct (Together AI) + Llama-3-8B-Instruct (1x A100); Llama-2 + Self-RAG stack (Table 2); GTR T5-large retriever, inner-product search; temp 0, zero-shot CoT, context capped 4096 (news)/2048 (conversations)
dataset_or_corpus: CLARK-News: 533 (subj,rel) Wikidata pairs, 1,174 changed triples (Nov 2021-Apr 2024, 10 relations, skewed: sports team 382 + position held 382 triples), 1,149 crowd-validated articles (680 US Prolific annotators, 2 human rounds + 1 LM round, NO IAA statistic), 1,409 template questions (time-free text; timestamp injected by inference prompt). CLARK-Conversations: 100 synthetic conversations x ~140 questions; 95% validation accuracy (3 authors, 3 conversations, 1,008 questions)
metrics: exact-match multiple-choice accuracy (alternatives = ALL answers true for the question past/present/future, so MC errors are version confusions by construction); set equality for list answers; questions re-asked at 20/40/60/80/100% ingestion checkpoints (all changed Q + equal-size unchanged Q'); conversations mean+-SE with significance bolding; news FIGURE-ONLY (no numeric table, no uncertainty)
main_findings: News: ERASE beats RAG/Fact-RAG/long-context by 7-13 (Mixtral) / 6-10 (Llama-3) points absolute (Fig.4); long-context fails to scale on news but full-context is the skyline on conversations; Table 2: Llama-2+SelfRAG 36.8%->47.9% with ERASE at ~6.6x less runtime (44:15->6:41); Table 3: single-hop edit gains significant, multi-hop remains hard (Llama-3 multi-hop 1-update 26.5+-0.2 vs RAG 22.2+-0.1); 0-update accuracy slightly DROPS under ERASE (editing noise on unchanged facts); Table 4 (old-target probe, camera-ready only): recovering initial-timestamp answers from the final KB degrades RAG 85.1->58.2 vs ERASE 85.9->64.8 (Mixtral, news)
limitations: Author (Limitations): multi-hop retrieval+editing weak; LM edits may introduce snowballing KB noise at scale; insertion-time cost justified only when insertions << queries. Reviewer: evidence NEVER experimentally controlled (natural chronological accumulation or LM-edited store); gold co-moves with ingestion (fn6: validity = article write/read time, not real-world change); main eval present-anchored (old target = single uncontrolled Table 4 probe, 1 model/domain, 2 systems); no attribution scoring; no abstention (MC forces choice); news results figure-only without uncertainty; Table 5 caption 'thirty' vs percentages implying denominator 20; camera-ready footnote 1 still anonymized
trust_dimensions: temporal currency of answers under streaming change; KB-maintenance quality (measured only via QA); forgetting of old answers (Table 4); NOT evidence faithfulness, NOT citation reliability, NOT calibration
evidence_intervention: none controlled: RAG arm = naturally accumulated chronological corpus; ERASE arm = incrementally LM-edited fact store; no old-only/new-only/mixed assignment, no condition-wise contrast; Table 4 decouples question time (initial) from store state (final) but over the uncontrolled natural mixture
abstention_evaluation: no (news MC has no abstain option; conversations list answers may be empty '[]' - a none-apply output, not scored abstention; no confidence/coverage/risk)
relevance_to_nr_specrag: Resolves CH-12 (last C1-adjacent lead): CLARK-News does NOT run controlled evidence-version conditions or answer-level version attribution, but camera-ready Table 4 is the FIRST historical-target evaluation in the reviewed literature (old-target novelty per se is dead); version-distractor MC makes version confusion the error mode by construction; dataset-level per-answer source attribution exists (Table 1 'attributed answers'). C1 wording must shift from 'old-target questions are unevaluated' to 'controlled evidence x target-version crossing with answer/citation-level attribution on normative specs is unevaluated'
